Arroyo claimed at the time that she was taking a shower when multiple armed men broke into the home and threatened them with a gun, demanding valuables.

Investigators now say that Arroyo was directly involved in the crime, as reported by the New York Post.

Arroyo was, in fact, in the home when the two men broke in. They demanded Van Dyke's PINs for his bank cards. He was tortured, beaten, and killed when he refused to give them the information.

The men then "stole" Arroyo's car after tying her up, which investigators said was just a cover.

What was the significance of this weekend's SpaceX tower catch: 

"Catching the second stage is substantially harder than catching the first stage because the Ship returns from orbit while the booster returns from a short suborbital hop. The booster separates minutes after liftoff, performs a brief boostback, and comes back from only a few hundred kilometers away at relatively low speed. Ship must reach orbital velocity, deploy payload, coast for many hours, execute a precise deorbit burn, survive full reentry heating, and only then perform its landing burn. As such, Ship must carry a functional heat shield, fly a long guided atmospheric trajectory from the other side of the planet, and execute a high-energy flip into the “chopsticks” while protecting its heat-shield side. Those combined demands of orbital energy, thermal protection, long-range guidance, and final precision are why a Ship catch is so incredibly difficult. No prior system, including the Space Shuttle, recovered a rocket-style orbital stage in this manner. The catch validates the path to full reusability which is the foundation of Starship’s cost and cadence targets. This is particularly important in driving the economics of orbital data centers." - DB
